summary: A child who grew up in an openly political home often took on the parents' party early and moved away from it once adult life added new voices.
realLife: A London School of Economics blog describes research on British and US households. Children from politically engaged homes were more likely to take on the parents' party view early, and also more likely to leave it in adulthood. The author ties this to university, work and new social networks. The same children updated their views more after major events such as a war or a scandal. The article gives no number for this.
sources: https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/europpblog/2013/05/17/children-with-politically-engaged-parents-are-more-likely-to-deviate-from-their-parents-political-views-in-adulthood/ (LSE EUROPP blog on parental politicization and later views)
